What a `run: proxy` step answers and when it fails: the type check, the headers sent, the size cap, an aborted stream, redirects and the log line.

The upstream's Content-Type is checked before anything is written. A type outside `content_types` (or missing, or application/octet-stream: the body is never sniffed), a Content-Encoding the client does not decode (it asks for gzip and decodes it, so a gzip answer streams decoded, with no Content-Length; br, deflate and others fail the step), a non-2xx status, a 204/205/206, or a declared Content-Length over `max_bytes` fails the step with nothing sent, so the flow's normal error handling answers (the 500 diagnostic, or an `on_error:` respond). The upstream body is never streamed on an error status.

A success answers 200 with the normalized allow-listed type (text/csv keeps only a utf-8, us-ascii, iso-8859-1 or windows-1252 charset), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` and a Content-Disposition. From the upstream only Content-Length (within the cap), ETag and Last-Modified pass; never Cache-Control, Expires, Set-Cookie or any other header.
Cache-Control: `private, no-store` unless the step declares `cache_control:` (see `proxy_keys`); the upstream's own Cache-Control and Expires are never passed on.

The first chunk of the body is read before the status is written. An upstream that sends its headers and then stalls or fails, the step's or flow's time running out, or a first chunk over `max_bytes` fails the step with nothing sent: the flow answers its normal error (the 500 diagnostic, a time-limit answer, or an `on_error:` handler), as for a refused type. The answer is never an empty 200, and a proxy in front never replays the request.

After the status and the first chunk are flushed, a body that passes `max_bytes`, an upstream read error, or the time running out ABORTS the connection: the caller sees a truncated, failed download (a network error), never a short body that looks complete, and a proxy in front passes the abort on rather than retrying. The step is not retried and its `on_error:` does not run once streaming has started. The app's request log records the request with the status sent and an error starting `response aborted`.

Redirects are followed for GET only, at most 10, and only on the URL's own origin (http to https on the same host counts); a redirect to another host, from https to http, or to another port, or any redirect of a POST, fails the step, and the error names which (reason `the upstream redirected outside the URL's own origin`). The URL is checked against private and internal addresses before the call, and so is every connection the call opens; a literal private host is refused when the file is written, in any spelling a resolver reads (`127.1`, `0x7f000001`, `2130706433`, `0177.0.0.1`, an IPv6 address with a zone). A host that does not resolve fails the step with `could not resolve the upstream host` (reason `the upstream host could not be resolved`).

Every upstream answer writes one log line (`FLOW PROXY [app] step=... host=... status=... type=... bytes=... outcome=sent|aborted|failed_before_body|refused_*`) with the host only, never the path, query or headers.
